papers.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
papers.abstract: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. We evaluate ASPIRE on three measured systems: a mobile robot, a rotational system with dry friction, and a laboratory fermenter. Each system is tested with and without a description, in five runs per task. All 30 runs delivered valid models, at a cost of 0.96 to 3.38 US dollars per run. An assessment by the authors found that, for the 30 models recommended by the agent, one per run, the interpretation of the model and the documentation of its structure selection and parameter estimation fully satisfied 132 of 150 assessed items and partly satisfied 18. The most frequent discrepancy, found in nine models, concerned inaccurate or unsupported claims about model structure selection.

papers.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
papers.abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $\pi_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

papers.title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

papers.title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
papers.abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

papers.title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) tracks the plan while discrete-time Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) on world-frame LiDAR points keep the robot clear of walls and unmapped obstacles. The algorithms live in a ROS-free, unit-tested core library, and the whole stack builds and runs from a single reproducible environment. In simulation, the robot drives a 135 m route through the maze with 1.0 cm localization RMSE against the known map and 24 cm in SLAM mode, the planner returns a path in 6 ms, and the NMPC solves in 11.7 ms on average, never exceeding its 80 ms budget.

papers.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
papers.abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at this https URL

papers.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
papers.abstract: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising. Using the relative reconstruction error of a frozen VDM denoiser as a probe, we find that conventional spatial encodings sit far off this prior, whereas frequency-domain packing yields latents that the denoiser corrects far less. Motivated by this diagnostic result, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame: each signal is assigned to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band and lifted to the spatial latent by an inverse DCT, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change. A fixed band layout together with slot-aware routing lets the same meta-frame support policy, world-model, and value prediction over a shared set of robot variables. On RoboCasa, MetaWAM reaches 68.9% success while collapsing the per-signal frames into one and cutting inference latency by 39%, and attains 85.0% success on three real-world Franka tasks. Code and models are available at this https URL

papers.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
papers.abstract: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap. We introduce an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that incorporates Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition (CLIFER) to personalize valence-arousal perception in real time. Differential feedback converts changes in valence-arousal direction and intensity into adjustments of the agent's target utility. An asynchronous architecture updates CLIFER in the background during live interaction. In a counterbalanced within-subject study in which 66 participants negotiated with a humanoid robot, the CL-enabled agent achieved significantly higher individual utility and elicited higher participant concession rates than the FaceChannel baseline. The CL condition yielded significantly higher mean arousal estimates, alongside a broader output range. Participant utility and Nash distance did not change significantly between conditions. These outcomes support the practical value of coupling continual affective personalization with differential feedback for real-time negotiation.

papers.title: HiPFuse: Real-Time LiDAR Semantic Segmentation for Robotic Perception on Edge Devices
papers.abstract: Real-time robotic perception requires accurate LiDAR semantics under limited resources. Bird's-eye-view (BEV) aggregation is efficient but can mix differently labeled surfaces in columns. We present HiPFuse, a point-BEV fusion framework that exchanges point and height-partitioned BEV features across horizontal scales, combining point-wise detail with 2D spatial context from one LiDAR scan. Fixed height assignments preserve separate vertical aggregation groups, with auxiliary supervision of initial BEV features using targets from the same 3D cells. A dual-scale BEV context module adds broader context from a coarser grid. On SemanticKITTI and MCD, HiPFuse achieves 63.7% and 62.5% mIoU at 14.2 and 22.4 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin, respectively, exceeding the 10 Hz scan rate. Separate training and evaluation show indoor applicability. Replacing only the baseline semantic front end with HiPFuse in fixed robotic systems reduces odometry absolute trajectory error RMSE by 10.6% on average across two outdoor sequences and increases accepted-loop recall by 8.7 percentage points on SemanticKITTI. Qualitative semantic maps show more continuous road labeling. Our code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
papers.abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

papers.title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional scene graphs (3DSGs) can provide robots with persistent metric-semantic representations for spatial reasoning, but the existing methods have primarily been developed for indoor and terrestrial environments. In this paper we investigate how a representative outdoor open-vocabulary method transfers to maritime environments and which adaptations are needed. Our experiments show that zero-shot representative outdoor 3DSG descriptions agree with our labeled ground truth for a majority of geometry-supported objects on our data, but the resulting map exhibits considerable physical-entity fragmentation, and its terrestrial higher-level assumptions don't capture maritime spatial organization needs. We therefore keep the underlying mapping method and post-process its accumulated evidence. We show a metric-semantic consolidation method followed by geometry-grounded multi-view vision-language model (VLM) reasoning that reconciles remaining fragments into physical entities and groups entities through observations into local places. In parallel, we construct maritime macro regions using map priors and onboard water and structure observations, and associate them with the local places. The resulting representation reduces physical-entity fragmentation beyond both the baseline and our geometry-semantic consolidation component alone, supports correspondence of fixed local places across repeated maritime traversals, and improves contextual retrieval on our reviewed queries over tested baselines. These results show how an outdoor open-vocabulary map can be adapted into persistent maritime scene memory with our methods for object/place identity and spatial abstractions.

papers.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
papers.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

papers.title: Oscillatory Processing Units as a computing substrate for biomimetic intelligence
papers.abstract: Biological intelligence emerges from neural activity that connects sensation, memory and action. Synaptic plasticity, neuronal assemblies and oscillations provide principles for biomimetic computing, but translating them into reusable operations requires a defined computational unit. We introduce Oscillatory Processing Units (OPUs), groups of synthetic neurons sharing a rhythm. Their directed interactions transform incoming activity and prior receiving state into an Oscillatory Occupancy Space (OOS), which becomes available to subsequent computation. We show that source--receiver conditions and oscillatory organization shape these transformations, including their geometry, persistence and historical accessibility. An Atlas of measured relationships supports prospective composition with predicted response classes. Configured circuits perform logical and numerical operations, express associative recall and generate closed-loop decisions with fixed synaptic weights. OPUs and OOS establish a computing substrate for biomimetic intelligence in which experience remains part of the state through which new input becomes action.

papers.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
papers.abstract: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over goals and embodied plans. Across several experiments spanning the qualitatively distinct domains of object manipulation and navigation, featuring diverse tasks and multiple behavioral measures, we show that GenEA, through simple transformations of this joint distribution, recapitulates how humans reason about embodied plans. Crucially, GenEA consistently outperforms strong alternative models, including plausible heuristics, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model. GenEA thereby offers a new perspective on the architecture of human reasoning and social cognition, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

papers.title: MouldIt: Data Efficiency of Multi-Task Temporal Representation Learning in Injection Moulding
papers.abstract: Smart industrial solutions that can address multiple tasks require models that understand the underlying processes. We examine representation learning for modeling the injection moulding process as an example of such solutions. We consider its data efficiency and multi-modal benefit compared to classical machine learning alternatives. To this end, we synthesize a process-informed dataset based on a real reference cycle of an Erlanger Träger part. We then introduce MouldIt, a temporal convolution and attention based variational autoencoder that reconstructs in-mould signals, while classifying parts as acceptable or as one of our synthetic failure modes. We evaluate MouldIt on two tasks, known-class classification and unknown-class detection, across nine dataset sizes in single-modal and multi-modal settings. We compare it with an accept-all baseline and the classical methods k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forests, and principal component analysis, which we adapt to support both tasks. MouldIt outperforms classical methods across both tasks from 4000 cycles in the single-modal setting and from 2000 cycles in the multi-modal setting. It achieves part sorting losses of 6.0 $\pm$ 0.7% and 1.0 $\pm$ 0.3% in the single-modal and multi-modal settings respectively, ranking first across all baselines and a combination of principal component analysis and random forests.

papers.title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
papers.abstract: Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $\pi_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. Across 30 policy inputs from 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, the Jacobian exhibits strong contracting directions near the action endpoint, yet no sampled mode violates the Euler non-expansion condition. On five of those inputs, accuracy sweeps require 4--9 Euler steps at 5% terminal error and 87--112 at 1%. These five paired cases are therefore consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.

papers.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
papers.abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

papers.topic_rationale: Coordinate-grounding VLM architecture for manipulation/planning, but not specifically mobile/dextrous/whole-body. Extensive comparative results on multiple grounding and embodied benchmarks.

executive_summary: Several works advance geometry- and navigation-oriented representations: DeRep pretrains a depth-based encoder using combined bird’s-eye-view reachability supervision and depth reconstruction, then freezes it for downstream policies, yielding lower linear policy prediction error, higher navigation success across linear probing, imitation learning, and PPO (beating purely reconstruction-based objectives in all six PPO conditions), and enabling zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments; UGG introduces a unified generative geometry model that jointly models RGB video, depth, and camera pose as conditional completions under modality- and time-dependent noise, learns from heterogeneous partially annotated datasets, supports search over multiple plausible 4D scene hypotheses, and outperforms non-unified baselines on camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and pose prediction, especially with sparse observations.

New planning and safety frameworks target robustness under uncertainty: L2P-DR-Forest is a sampling-based motion planner for nonlinear stochastic systems that learns optimal-transport-based ambiguity sets over unknown initial and process noise distributions, propagates them through dynamics, and checks safety, with proofs that returned plans satisfy specifications with prescribed confidence and are probabilistically complete under added assumptions, and empirical outperformance of existing stochastic planners; DOBB defines Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes that translate each agent’s state, uncertainty, and response into direction-dependent safety margins used for decentralized learning-based collision avoidance, achieving a 2.6% mean total failure rate across four multi-agent environments with collision failures ≤2.3% even under out-of-distribution actuation and estimation shifts; LBS proposes Latent Barrier Steering for generative planning, first steering behavior latents toward higher safety margins and then applying a path-space control-barrier-function QP, which increases safety margins, offers finite-time recovery guarantees, and reduces correction effort while maintaining safety and improving goal-reaching over path-only filters; SIGMO introduces a sigmoid-gated, interaction-aware driving planner that computes physics-grounded yield scores via polynomial sigmoids for surrounding agents and embeds them in a receding-horizon planner, remaining computationally lightweight while balancing proactive and defensive actions to avoid freezing and over-conservatism in simulation and hardware driving scenarios.

Several systems enhance physically grounded control and locomotion: GRF-MPC incorporates live ground reaction forces and center-of-pressure into a human centroidal-dynamics model and solves a real-time QP under an underactuated 4-cable configuration, where, versus a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance controller in ~300 trials with six participants, it reduces peak planar CoM error by 19.6%, trajectory tracking error by 24.1%, and net mechanical work by 28.7% while increasing normalized voluntary excursion area by 45.9% at 100 Hz replanning; a nonlinear 6-DoF MPCC for holonomic AUVs augments nominal dynamics with Gaussian-Process-learned residuals via a zero-order robust optimization that preserves 25 Hz real-time control, with simulation ablations highlighting residual selection and combined simulations/in-water experiments on the MOLA AUV showing better constrained trajectory tracking than nominal MPCC and a field-proven PID; ReACT is a humanoid locomotion framework that uses reflection-consistent disturbance modulation and cross-load tracking consistency training to preserve action correspondence under mirrored, asymmetrically loaded conditions, improving velocity tracking and reducing directional bias under varying asymmetric loads in simulation and achieving collision-free goal reaching in all 40 real-world navigation trials with unilateral hand loads.

Task-level autonomy is extended to complex manipulation and process planning: Curie’s Jarvis enables a Franka Panda to execute chemistry protocols from photos of printed instructions on unstructured benches without fiducials, locating and label-reading visually similar containers from four camera views, autonomously completing 5/5 runs of one children’s kit and 4/5 of another and correctly identifying all containers in 160 printed/handwritten-label trials; DexSeed converts human hand–object interaction data into low-cost dexterous robot demonstrations by clustering by grasp mode with shared language, retargeting via InteractionMesh, augmenting arm trajectories, and using an RL finger controller in simulation to generate labeled rollouts for fine-tuning a vision-language-action model that, in simulation and real world, executes language-specified grasps, with experiments reporting improved contact fidelity and more reliable whole-arm execution than baselines; an offline optimization-based path planner for industrial manipulators unifies joint-path regularity, self-collision penalties, and process-specific costs/constraints using full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization with Iterative Weight Tuning from KPI–target gaps, and on UR10e carbon-fiber winding and 3D printing tasks produces hardware-executable paths that satisfy geometric tolerances and meet all KPI targets (with printing evaluated without extrusion); a deployment adaptation method for next-best-view selection learns a local sensor-return adapter atop a fixed pretrained world model to estimate measurement dropout, leading in real-robot structured-light experiments to higher surface coverage with 60% fewer captures and successful recovery of a surface region that a nominal strategy repeatedly targets but fails to measure.

Language and cognitive-style models are applied to planning and explanation: an uncertainty-aware lunar rover assistant couples a large language model with a sampling-based planner via a ReAct-style tool interface to explain trajectories in domain terms and re-run planning under user-specified conditions; in a simulator inspired by NASA’s VIPER mission and evaluated on plan comparison, feasibility, and lookup queries, this tool-augmented setup achieves 90.9% response faithfulness to planner outputs, nearly a 65% improvement over zero-shot prompting of the same LLM without tools; GenEA defines a generative agent with a multilevel state space linking articulated body biomechanics and object interactions, extending task-and-motion planning with simulation-based intuitive physics to obtain a joint distribution over goals and embodied plans whose transformations, across manipulation and navigation tasks, are reported to reproduce human reasoning about plans and to consistently outperform heuristic models, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model.

New generative and streaming frameworks target expressive robot behaviors: AHEADance is a real-time dance generation system for humanoids that uses ListenAhead to condition motion chunks on past audio and a frozen music model’s future-audio forecasts, weighted by reliability and time-aligned to motion; forecasted features preserving beat timing improve synchronization and focus motion energy at the beat frequency, while Commit Forcing (training continuations from the model’s own committed chunks) reduces low-activity motion from 83.5% to 10.3%, aligning with real dance data, and a Unitree G1 deployment demonstrates online, beat-synchronized dancing that starts and stops with the music without falls.

institution_matches.title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes DeRep, a depth-based navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird’s-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction, with encoders pretrained and then frozen for downstream policy learning. Across linear policy probing, flow-matching imitation learning, and PPO-based reinforcement learning, DeRep yields lower linear policy prediction error and higher navigation success than depth reconstruction-only objectives in all six tested PPO conditions, while reachability-based objectives in imitation learning achieve higher mean success rates than reconstruction alone. A PPO policy using a frozen DeRep encoder is deployed without fine-tuning in Gazebo and on a physical quadrotor, demonstrating zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer in cluttered navigation tasks.

institution_matches.title: Learn-To-Propagate: Distributionally Robust Motion Planning for Nonlinear Uncertain Systems
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces Learn-To-Propagate Distributionally-Robust Forest (L2P-DR-Forest), a sampling-based motion planning algorithm for nonlinear stochastic systems with unknown initial state and process noise distributions, using optimal-transport-based learned ambiguity sets that are propagated through the dynamics and checked for safety. The authors prove that L2P-DR-Forest is correct in the sense that every returned plan satisfies the specifications with prescribed confidence and, under additional feasibility and distributional assumptions, is probabilistically complete. Evaluations on several robotic benchmarks indicate that L2P-DR-Forest significantly outperforms existing motion planning methods for stochastic systems while providing high-confidence formal guarantees.

institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes UGG, a unified generative geometry model that jointly models RGB video, depth, and camera pose by treating visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion under differing noise levels across modalities and time. UGG’s unified generative formulation allows learning from heterogeneous datasets with partial geometric or visual annotations and supports inference-time search over multiple plausible 4D scene hypotheses using geometric cues extracted from observed RGB frames. Experiments show that UGG outperforms non-unified baselines on camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, particularly in sparse observation scenarios.

topic_matches.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), which incorporates live ground reaction force and center-of-pressure measurements into a human centroidal dynamics model and solves a real-time quadratic program to optimize assistive forces and moments for upright physical assistance with a cable-driven robot. Implemented on the RobUST trainer in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and compared to a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance controller over nearly 300 trials with six healthy participants, GRF-MPC reduces peak planar CoM error during perturbations by 19.6%, lowers trajectory tracking error by 24.1%, requires 28.7% less net mechanical work, and increases normalized voluntary excursion area by 45.9%. The underlying quadratic program solves in under 1 ms, enabling 100 Hz replanning and demonstrating that incorporating live human–ground interaction into predictive control can provide stronger, more transparent assistance with fewer actuators.

topic_matches.title: Incorporating World Models in Decision Making for Next Best View Selection in Active Sensing
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes a deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection in robotic 3D reconstruction that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping a pretrained world model fixed, estimating measurement dropout over predicted surfaces to guide view selection. In real-robot experiments with a structured-light sensor, the adapted next-best-view method achieves higher measured surface coverage with 60% fewer captures than the nominal selection strategy and successfully recovers a surface region that the nominal method repeatedly targets but fails to measure.

topic_matches.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces AHEADance, a streaming dance generation system for humanoid robots that uses ListenAhead to condition each motion chunk on past audio and a frozen music model’s forecasts of future audio, weighted by reliability and time-aligned to target motion segments. Using forecasted music features that preserve beat timing, ListenAhead improves synchronization and concentrates motion energy at the song’s beat frequency, while Commit Forcing—training continuation from the model’s own committed chunks—reduces low-activity motion from 83.5% to 10.3%, matching the low-activity level of real dance data. Deployed on a physical Unitree G1 humanoid, AHEADance produces online, beat-synchronized dancing that starts and stops with the music without causing the robot to fall.

topic_matches.title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
topic_matches.institution: Eastern Institute of Technology; National University of Singapore; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents ReACT, a humanoid locomotion framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads, combining reflection-consistent disturbance modulation—using estimated wrenches to modulate actor features while preserving action correspondence under mirrored observations—with cross-load tracking consistency training that aligns tracking performance between loaded and unloaded conditions. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid demonstrate improved velocity tracking and reduced directional bias across varying asymmetric loads, and real-world tests show collision-free goal reaching in all 40 navigation trials under unilateral hand loads using a fixed mapless navigation policy.

topic_matches.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes an offline optimization-based path planner for industrial manipulators that unifies joint-path regularity, self-collision penalties, and process-specific costs and constraints, using full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization plus Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) to set cost weights from KPI–target gaps. In experiments on carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing with a UR10e, the planned joint paths satisfy the specified geometric tolerances and meet all KPI targets, and are executable on hardware (with joint-level tracking recorded and printing performed without extrusion).

topic_matches.title: DexSeed: Expanding Human Hand-Object Interactions into Robot Demonstrations for Dexterous Policy Learning
topic_matches.institution: Robbyant; The University of Hong Kong; Zhejiang University
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces DexSeed, a framework that generates low-cost dexterous robot demonstrations from human hand–object interaction data by grouping sequences by grasp mode with shared language descriptions, retargeting them via InteractionMesh, augmenting arm trajectories, and using an RL finger-control policy with arm-tracking dynamics in physics simulation. Rendered visual observations and recorded robot actions from successful simulated rollouts are paired with grasp-language descriptions to fine-tune a vision-language-action (VLA) model, which in simulation and real-world deployment can execute language-specified grasps using only these generated demonstrations. Experiments indicate that DexSeed improves contact fidelity in retargeting and yields more reliable whole-arm execution compared to evaluated baselines in simulation.

topic_matches.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
topic_matches.institution: KTH Royal Institute of Technology; The Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI)
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents a nonlinear 6-DoF Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) scheme for a holonomic AUV that augments a nominal dynamics model with residual dynamics learned via Gaussian Process regression, incorporated through a zero-order robust optimization formulation to maintain 25 Hz real-time control. Simulation ablations show that appropriate residual selection is critical to controller design, and combined simulation and in-water experiments on the MOLA AUV demonstrate that the GP-augmented MPCC outperforms a nominal MPCC and a field-proven PID controller for constrained trajectory tracking.

topic_matches.title: SIGMO: Sigmoid Gated Interaction-Aware Motion Planning
topic_matches.institution: Honda Research Institute, USA, Inc.; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes SIGMO, a sigmoid-gated interaction-aware motion planner that analytically computes yield scores for surrounding agents using physics-grounded interaction features via polynomial sigmoid functions, and embeds these scores in a receding-horizon planner that can use arbitrary trajectory predictions. Simulation and hardware experiments in interaction-intensive driving scenarios indicate that SIGMO remains computationally lightweight while balancing proactive and defensive behaviors, avoiding both freezing and overly conservative navigation, and providing a strong baseline for autonomous driving mobility stacks.

topic_matches.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes (DOBB), an online geometric safety representation that converts each agent’s current state estimate, uncertainty, and response characteristics into a direction-dependent safety margin, and derives interaction features and a reward function that preserve the physical meaning of these margins for decentralized learning-based collision avoidance. Across four multi-agent evaluation environments, DOBB-based policies achieve a lowest reported mean total failure rate of 2.6%, with collision-based failure remaining at or below 2.3% under tested out-of-distribution shifts in actuation dynamics and state-estimation uncertainty. The authors attribute the robustness of DOBB-based collision avoidance under uncertainty and heterogeneous dynamics to its geometric abstraction of safety margins, which reduces coupling between learned behavior and the specific uncertainty and actuation regimes seen during training.

topic_matches.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical framework for flow-matching-based generative planning that first steers a behavior latent toward trajectories with larger safety margins, then applies a path-space control-barrier-function (CBF) quadratic program to correct any remaining safety violations. By separating behavior selection from path certification, latent steering in LBS increases the available safety margin for the path-space CBF corrector, providing finite-time recovery guarantees and reducing the correction burden compared with approaches that only filter trajectories at the path level. Experiments on navigation and robot end-effector planning tasks show that LBS maintains safety while improving goal-reaching performance and lowering correction effort relative to pure path-level safety filters applied to generative planners.
